URL: https://www.cityam.com/end-of-triple-lock-what-is-the-double-lock-and-will-it-work/
City AM (Maisie Grice) — published 2026-09-29T16:15:47Z, confirmed from article metadata. Search highlights.
Triple lock remains for the rest of this parliament, changed in April 2030 if Labour wins the next general election.
OBR: if left unchanged, the cost of the state pension would balloon by more than £15bn per year by 2030.
IFS: spending on the state pension is £16bn a year higher because of the triple lock.
RACHEL VAHEY, head of public policy, AJ Bell: "The idea that scrapping the triple lock will bankroll social care on its own is simply fantasy." "There's a mismatch between one policy - scrapping the triple lock guarantee, saving a little over a long period of time - and another, introducing a social care system costing a lot immediately."
JONATHAN CRIBB, deputy director, IFS: "The savings to the Exchequer from this reform are likely to be relatively small in the first few years." "However, over time the new triple lock will prevent the state pension being locked into an ever-increasing level of generosity compared with workers' earnings, thereby generating significant savings in the long run."
IFS formulation of the new lock: the new state pension would increase by the maximum of CPI inflation, 2.5 per cent, or "the amount needed to ensure the state pension keeps up with average earnings growth since the introduction of the new policy".
TOMM ADAMS, partner, Blick Rothenberg: Burnham left a "fair amount of detail unspoken", but the PM could be waiting for "the Treasury and OBR to do the full costing".
